- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early forecast periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d forecast); apply smoothing or lagged trend correction.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model reacts with lag; adjust forecast 1–3 days ahead to align with sentiment reversal.
- For 30d forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation; if sentiment is volatile, use 10–15% buffer for volatility in mid-to-late horizon.
